messages.subject: unmarkedFrameOccuMulti - obsCovs
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to fit models for a couple of species. Therefore I am using the unmarkedFrameOccuMulti function to create an umf object. However, when I try to incorporates the obsCovs (e.g. camera.model - this is the different models of cameratraps I am using) I get the following error message: 

"Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “unmarkedFrameOccuMulti” object: obsCovData does not have M*obsNum rows."

I am not quite sure how to interpret this. 

The obsCovs were selected from a .csv containing variables for 55 different sites (hence 55 rows) and also the covariates I used to create siteCovs (which are working fine) I am not sure what the problem is. 

In addition, I am not sure what I need to indicate in J<- #number of visits as these vary from camera to camera (some may have turned off before collection) - do I need to average the number of days they were active? Min 2 Max 14 days of cameras in operation.

Thank you very much.

Best,
Ettore.

messages.author: bd00314644d53a96
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarkedFrameOccuMulti - obsCovs
parts:
Hello,

It's probably because your variable is a site covariate (SiteCov), not an observation variable (ObsCov). Observation variables (ObsCov) are those that vary between each sampling event and sometimes for each site. While site variables only vary for each station. 
In this case you mention that your csv has 55 rows and I imagine one column per variable, so the error is that you should have a matrix with the same dimensions as your detection/non-detection history matrix.  In the case you had an observation variable, like the moon phase or daily weather conditions, it should have 55 rows and the same number of columns as the sampling events you defined. 
I hope it was clear, but if not you can look at this article from Guillera-Arroita 2017 ,where the definition of the types of covariates is explained very well, and which ones affect each process.
